reason: I'll combine the bones to start building the arm's framework.
expectation: I expect a connected arm framework, though it may still need joint surfaces and support.

alternatives.reason: The cartilage and fluid also seem relevant to the joint, but I want to establish the framework first.

effect: The bones provide rigid supports but still need a joint where they can move relative to each other.
reaction: The distinction between bending bones and movement at a joint is clear.
reason: Cartilage and joint fluid are the only offered combination and seem relevant to making smooth joint surfaces.
expectation: I expect them to form a smooth joint surface or cushioning, though I'm unsure exactly how they will be combined.

effect: The cartilage covers bone ends and the fluid helps them slide; the next goal is to join the framework and attach the muscles.
reaction: The different roles of cartilage and fluid make the joint easier to picture.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should add the smooth surfaces to the arm bones.
expectation: I expect the bone ends to gain smooth joint surfaces, though the joint may still need ligaments and muscles.

effect: The joint surfaces let the forearm turn, but the articulated bones still need support and a pulling force.
reaction: The distinction between permitting movement and producing it is clear.
reason: Ligaments are the only offered combination and seem useful for supporting the joint.
expectation: I expect the ligaments to help hold the articulated bones together while allowing the elbow to move.

effect: The ligaments hold the joint together, and the framework now has slots for the opposing muscle pulls.
reaction: The distinction between ligaments connecting bones and muscles producing pulls is useful.
reason: I'll attach the bending muscles to begin filling the framework's pull slots.
expectation: I expect the bending muscles to fill the front pull slot, leaving the rear pull to attach.

alternatives.reason: The straightening muscles also need attaching, but either side seems reasonable to start with.

effect: The bending muscles pull through tendons, and relaxing them does not push the bones back. The framework still needs the opposing muscles.
reaction: The explanation makes the need for an opposing pull clear.
reason: The straightening muscles are the only offered combination and should complete the opposing arrangement.
expectation: I expect the straightening muscles to fill the rear pull slot and let the arm straighten.

effect: The opposing muscles complete the framework and can bend, straighten or steady the joint; coordinating them remains another job.
reaction: The example of holding a weight still added an interesting use for muscle force.

mostWorthwhile.text: Attaching the bending muscles was most worthwhile because the explanation connected tendons to movement and clarified why an opposing pull is needed.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the smooth surfaces to the bones felt somewhat repetitive: it was the only offered combination, and the result mostly confirmed that the joint permits movement.

surprise.text: I was interested that muscles can keep pulling without shortening, such as when holding a weight still.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; even the forced combinations had clear purposes in assembling the joint.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the opposing muscles are coordinated, although this chapter had few meaningful choices.
